subject: FintechAI — follow-up: pricing & latency trade-offs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@fintechai.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: FintechAI — follow-up: pricing & latency trade-offs

Hi Ava / team — great to speak today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our discovery call so we’re aligned on assumptions before I hand this to pricing/procurement: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Primary use: real-time transaction enrichment + customer-facing chat (low-latency requirement for the latter).
- Expected token volumes: 30M–60M tokens/month in Q2, ramping to ~150M tokens/month within 6–9 months if pilot goes well.
- Budget target: initial target range $1,500–$3,000 / 1M tokens (total budget band $45k–$180k/month depending on ramp).
- Latency SLO goal: p95 <= 200ms for chat; background enrichment can tolerate 500–800ms.

Key trade-offs we discussed
- Latency vs cost: lower-p95 targets (150–200ms) typically require higher-tier instances or dedicated capacity; cost-optimized modes (batching, higher token packing, quantized models) can cut unit cost but add tail latency.
- Streaming vs batch: streaming keeps tail latency predictable for chat but reduces batching efficiency; for enrichment you can use batched endpoints to save 30–60% on per-token cost.

Immediate options I’ll prepare for you
1) Hosted Premium (low p95): target ~150ms p95; blended price estimate in the $3,000 / 1M tokens range for initial volumes, with discounts at scale. Best for customer-facing chat.
2) Cost-optimized Hosted: p95 ~350–500ms; price estimate ~$1,500 / 1M tokens. Use aggressive batching, KV prefix caching, and quantized variants for enrichment pipelines.
3) Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput, can hit <150ms p95 with lower blended unit cost at higher commitments; we’ll model a committed monthly price for a 6–12 month term.

Next steps
- I’ll send a detailed cost breakout and two benchmark scenarios (chat streaming vs batched enrichment) — aim to have that by tomorrow EOD.
- Can you confirm the procurement contact and whether FintechAI requires an NDA before we share the SOW/benchmarks? (I’ve CC’d Rishi who will help on SLA and SOW.)

Thanks — Marissa

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FintechAI — follow-up: pricing & latency trade-offs

Ava — attached the detailed materials I promised: redwood-pricing-sheet-q1-2027.pdf (pricing bands + unit economics), benchmark-500ms-vs-150ms.csv (benchmark runs and config), and a rough SOW draft (sow-draft-fintechai.docx). Highlights below so procurement has quick answers: 

Assumptions used for estimates
- Model: 13B open checkpoint (quantized where applicable) for enrichment; 30B optimized variant for low-latency chat in premium tier.
- Avg tokens per call: chat 120 tokens; enrichment 450 tokens.
- Request mix for pilot: 60% chat, 40% enrichment.

Representative unit economics (pilot volumes 30M tokens/month)
- Hosted Premium (streaming, low-p95): $3,200 / 1M tokens -> ~$96k/month
- Hosted Cost-Optimized (batched, quantized): $1,700 / 1M tokens -> ~$51k/month
- Dedicated (reserved, 12mo commit): blended effective $1,400 / 1M tokens at 120M tokens/mo commit -> ~$168k/month (with predictable SLAs)

Notes on knobs to tune cost vs latency
- Batch size: larger batches reduce $/token but increases p95; we recommend adaptive batching for chat to keep p95 under SLO while batching enrichment aggressively.
- Streaming: keeps first-byte latency low for chat; reduces batching efficiency by ~20–30% on same hardware.
- Cache & prefixes: for repeated prompts we can reduce token counts and cost by up to 15–25% depending on reuse.

Attached files are the ones listed in my CC. Procurement — I included our standard T&Cs and SOC2 evidence link in the SOW draft. If you prefer, we can send the SOC2 report under an NDA. 

Proposed next steps:
- Internal: Rishi to review SLA language & confirm whether we can offer a p95 200ms pilot SLA under a hosted agreement or if dedicated capacity is required.
- External: schedule 30-min technical benchmark review with your ML infra lead (I’ll propose slots).

If you want a straw-man quote with exact line items I can push that to you today — let me know which pricing band you want modeled (premium vs cost-optimized vs dedicated).

Thanks — Marissa

Ava / team — quick note from engineering/SRE side:

- For a p95 <= 200ms on chat at 30M tokens/month, hosted premium with our optimized 30B variant + streaming is feasible for pilot, but the cost will be at the higher band Marissa outlined. If you expect to ramp quickly to 120–150M, we should model dedicated pools — it’s more cost-effective at scale and gives headroom for steady p95.
- SLO-driven pricing option: we can structure a pilot where pricing is tiered based on achieved p95 (e.g., base price for <=350ms, premium uplift if you require <=200ms SLO). This helps trade risk and gives you a runbook to move from hosted -> dedicated as needed.
- Operational knobs: adaptive batching, KV prefix caching, and autoscaling warm pools. I recommend we run a 2-day benchmark with your sample payloads to produce a reproducible cost vs latency matrix we can include in the SOW.

Action items
- Marissa: please send the benchmark CSV and SOW to Procurement (attached).
- Ava: share ML infra sample prompts + a 24-hour traffic profile for the benchmark run.
- Ben: can you create the HubSpot quote for FIN-2384 (pilot) and include the tiered SLO pricing option?

Happy to jump on a call with your ML infra lead this week for the benchmark kick-off.

Best — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
